title: Compact-surface button: press-shear micro-animation, adaptive hitbox, and deferred spinner strategy
creator: Avery Chen
description: Problem: Compact and icon-only buttons are inconsistent across products: hit targets vary, press feedback feels heavy on dense surfaces, and spinners either jump layout or feel visually noisy. Several regressions were introduced after recent spinner token updates (DES-74123, DES-95314) leading to visual jank on narrow toolbars and mobile. Goal: create a cohesive compact-surface button pattern that (1) preserves layout stability, (2) offers subtle but clear press feedback for touch and pointer, (3) improves accessibility semantics for icon-only controls, and (4) introduces a deferred spinner that avoids flicker for short operations.
acceptance_criteria: New compact-surface button component includes an optional 'press-shear' micro-animation (max 22ms translate+scale) that feels tactile without shifting layout.
Icon-only buttons have consistent 40px visual tap target with an adaptive hitbox that expands on pointerdown only (no permanent layout padding).
Loading spinner is deferred: only swaps to visual spinner after 350ms; before that the button shows a subtle progressive fill overlay to indicate work without layout shift.
All changes are token-driven (new tokens added: button.compact.press-translate, button.loading.defer-ms, button.icon.hitbox-offset, button.loading.fill-color) and documented in the tokens spec.

Keyboard and screen-reader semantics preserved: icon controls expose aria-label/aria-pressed where applicable; spinner state exposed via aria-busy on the button and an offscreen label for live region updates.
Reduced-motion preference disables the shear animation and replaces it with an immediate 0.97 scale-on-press for motion-sensitive users.
No visual regressions on existing button variants in dark/light themes; cross-browser QA cleared on Chrome, Safari, Firefox (desktop and mobile) with CI visual diffs below threshold.
Implementation PR includes Storybook stories for: default, compact, icon-only, loading-deferred, reduced-motion, RTL, and high-contrast states.
Design handoff artifacts (Figma components, tokens table, annotated spec) are linked and reviewed by ENG and PM.
Rollout plan includes feature flag gated launch and staged migration of current icon-button usages over 2 sprints with monitoring dashboard for UI regressions.
Update related docs: component library README, changelog, and migration notes for teams using custom CSS overrides.
design_notes: Press-shear concept: combine a tiny translateY (1-2px) with a -2% scaleX to simulate lateral press shear on compact surfaces. Limit duration to 80ms total; easing cubic-bezier(.2,.9,.2,1) for snappy return.

Adaptive hitbox: visually keep the 32px icon compact but expand interactive area to 40px using pointer-event only layer on pointerdown. On pointer up/tap the hitbox collapses back to visual bounds. This avoids layout shifts and preserves density.

Deferred spinner: show a transparent progressive fill overlay (using token button.loading.fill-color at 12% opacity) that animates left-to-right for the first 350ms. If call still pending at 350ms, fade overlay out and fade spinner in with crossfade (150ms).

Token changes: propose these new semantic tokens so teams can override them per theme: button.compact.press-translate, button.compact.press-scale, button.icon.hitbox-target, button.loading.defer-ms, button.loading.fill-color, button.loading.spinner-size.

Visual density story: ensure compact-surface options exist at 32/36/40 visual sizes with clear mapping from tokens to CSS variables to support platform parity (web, react-native-web, and mobile SDKs).

Edge-case: when icon+label combos collapse under width constraints, button should gracefully switch to icon-only compact with aria-expanded if applicable (handled in component composition, not design token).
accessibility_notes: Expose loading via aria-busy='true' on the button element while operation pending; also include an offscreen live region text like 'Saving...' for SR users when spinner becomes visible.
Ensure icon-only buttons always have an aria-label or aria-labelledby; add guide text to PRD and component docs with a linter rule recommendation.
Test with NVDA and VoiceOver: spinner crossfade should not cause duplicate announcements; prefer live region updates only when state meaningfully changes.
Reduced-motion: follow prefers-reduced-motion media query. Remove translate animation and rely on instant opacity/scale changes for press feedback.
Hitbox expansion must not interfere with adjacent touch targets—when pointerdown expands hitbox, ensure pointer capture semantics are used so surrounding elements don't receive unintended events.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Design): finalize Figma tokens and component variants; get ENG/PM sign-off (this ticket).
Phase 1 (Flagged PR): ENG implements under feature flag 'compact-press-shear' with Storybook examples. Run visual diff tests and accessibility smoke tests.
Phase 2 (Canary): Enable flag for 10% of internal users and specific product page routes; monitor console errors, layout regressions, and user-reported flakiness for 2 weeks.
Phase 3 (Gradual): Toggle on for all internal builds and then external release per regular cadence. Provide migration guide for teams consuming legacy CSS variables.
Rollback: Revert feature flag and CSS token mapping; keep legacy tokens available for 3 releases to ease migration.
qa_checks: Visual diff: no >5px shift in layout for any existing page where buttons are used after token change.
Interaction: press-shear animation triggers on pointerdown and completes on pointerup within 120ms total.
Loading behavior: spinner appears only after 350ms and spinner crossfade timing matches spec.
Keyboard nav: buttons reachable via Tab and press animation triggered by Space/Enter with same semantics as pointer.
Screen reader: aria-busy and live region behave as specified; no duplicate announcements.
High contrast: tokens deliver accessible contrast ratios >= 4.5:1 for primary actions and >= 3:1 for secondary variants as defined in DS guidelines.
Mobile: touch target behavior verified on iOS Safari and Android Chrome; no accidental gestures caused by hitbox expansion.
